exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal vs. caesarean section)
outcome: Active force capacity of levator ani muscle
Pelvic floor dysfunction symptoms (bladder dysfunction, prolapse symptoms, sexual dysfunction symptoms)
cohort: 59 nulliparous women with singleton, low-risk pregnancies
finding: While active force of the levator ani muscle significantly decreased during pregnancy and postpartum, muscle stiffness only decreased in women who had vaginal deliveries.
mod_finding: Postpartum muscle stiffness differed significantly between women who gave birth vaginally and those who had a caesarean section.
